body.heading: Show up in low-key ways
paragraphs: Hard weeks shrink people's energy for replying, planning, and even accepting help. So keep your offers light: a message that needs no answer, food left at the door, a walk with no agenda.
'No need to reply' might be the kindest four words in a hard week. They give support without adding one more obligation to a full plate.

body.heading: Stay after the crisis
paragraphs: Support floods in during the first days of bad news, then quietly disappears while the hard part is still going. The friend who checks in three weeks later, when everyone else has moved on, is the one people remember.
Put a reminder in your phone if you have to. Remembering later is a skill, and it is allowed to use tools.

description: You cannot fix a friend's hard week, but you can make it noticeably less lonely.
